turns.zh: 好的，很高兴见到大家。我叫 Noah，在 AI 部署团队。整个演示过程中，大家随时可以在聊天区提问。我会回答这些问题，也会把一些话题抛给你们。

turns.en: Amazing. I wanted to start with a big change which I think we are probably all well aware of, which is not only is product management, the craft of product management, changing, but so too is the way in which everybody is building software. And so I really like this DHH quote off the Lex Fridman podcast recently, the developer's developer, I think really capturing sort of this moment, which is software is product management. What should the product do? Who should it do it for? How should it do it? How should it look? And what are the priorities? These are all questions that now everybody is capable of wrestling with as we start to build products and software. Everybody can be thinking like a product manager. And so very excited to talk about Grok Bot and the ways that we've been using it on the SpaceX AI product team. And so with that, wanted to share a little backdrop of why we built Grok Bot.
turns.zh: 太好了。我想从一个很大的变化说起，这个变化我们大概都清楚，那就是不仅产品管理这门手艺在变，所有人构建软件的方式也在变。我特别喜欢 DHH 最近在 Lex Fridman 播客上的那句话，这位“开发者的开发者”我觉得很好地抓住了这个时刻，那就是“软件即产品管理”。产品该做什么？为谁而做？怎么做？该长什么样？优先级是什么？这些问题是现在每个人在构建产品和软件时都有能力去琢磨的。每个人都可以像产品经理一样思考。所以非常兴奋能聊聊 Grok Bot，以及我们在 SpaceX AI 产品团队里是怎么用它的。那么接下来，我想先分享一下我们为什么要做 Grok Bot 的背景。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. So I thought it'd be helpful to just kick off with some general context and kind of why Grok Bot exists. And we're thinking about this when putting this together, and a few themes sort of came up, and a lot of this was inspired by our internal usage as well as what we heard from a bunch of customers over the history of building our products ourselves. And I think a few themes emerged. One of those first ones is that it sort of increasingly felt that you wanted to work with agents and those agents weren't quite at home in a chat box. I think the chat box is actually really great. I use chat boxes all the time. Really enjoy them for all kinds of interactivity with LLMs and AI workflows, but for something about agents getting work done, it felt a little bit limiting and constraining. And so really wanting to think about what the right interface is and the right way to interact with an agent would be. And I also think if you kind of contextualize that to product management work, this becomes even more salient, right? Like PMs are often trying to focus on outcomes. You're often working across multiple parts of the stack. So you're coordinating with various different functions at a company. You're like kind of a general manager. You're kind of thinking about design. You're thinking about analytics a lot. You're working with engineering. And you'll see a little bit about that and how we've set it up in the demo later on. But really that PM work in particular seems to go beyond this Q&A format that is really native for the chat box. The other thing that was a really sort of emerging theme is that agents really need their own environments to get work done. We actually saw a lot of this with cloud agents early on, where giving agents the ability to verify their work and verify their output results in dramatically better outcomes. And so the idea was, well, what's the natural extension of that? And I think it's giving agents their own environments to do the work in. And I think the more we started experimenting and playing with that, the more we saw that that could be a really powerful thing too. The last thing I wanted to mention here is that it gets really hard to babysit multiple agent threads. We had a lot of folks internally who had built their own sort of coordinator agent that was then calling out to other agents, but that wasn't ever really done in a really first-class way across products. And we think Grok Bot does a pretty good job at this, but really this idea of, as you're thinking about multitasking, you're switching between meeting one over here on this topic to meeting two over here on that topic, having some way to just keep track of all the mess that goes on in a normal workday. And I think we increasingly just started to think of ourselves as, well, what if we could work with our agents more like colleagues versus working with them more like software? And that was kind of the design brief for a lot of what Grok Bot is.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得先讲一些总体背景、讲讲 Grok Bot 为什么存在会很有帮助。我们在筹备这次分享时就在想这些，浮现出了几个主题，很多灵感来自我们内部的使用，也来自我们过去自己做产品时从很多客户那里听到的反馈。我觉得有几个主题浮现出来。第一个是，人们越来越想和智能体一起工作，而这些智能体在聊天框里并不太自在。其实聊天框非常棒，我一直在用聊天框，很喜欢用它和 LLM 做各种交互、跑各种 AI 工作流，但要让智能体真正把活干完，聊天框就有点局限、有点束缚了。所以我们真的很想思考，什么才是和智能体交互的正确界面、正确方式。而且如果你把它放到产品管理工作的语境里，这就更明显了，对吧？产品经理往往专注于结果，经常要跨多个层面工作，要和公司里各种不同职能协调，有点像总经理，要思考设计，要大量思考分析，还要和工程团队合作。后面演示里你们会看到一点我们是怎么设置的。但产品管理这项工作，似乎确实超出了聊天框那种原生的一问一答格式。另一个逐渐浮现的主题是，智能体真的需要自己的环境来干活。我们早期在云端智能体上就看到了很多这一点：让智能体能够验证自己的工作、验证输出结果，会带来好得多的结果。所以想法就是，那自然的延伸是什么？我认为就是给智能体自己的环境去干活。我们越开始实验、越玩这个，就越发现这可能是一件非常强大的事。最后我想提的一点是，同时照看多个智能体线程真的很难。我们内部有很多人自己搭了某种协调智能体，再去调用其他智能体，但这从来没有在产品层面被真正做成一等公民。我们认为 Grok Bot 在这方面做得不错，但核心想法是，当你在多任务处理时，从这个话题的会议一切换到那个话题的会议二，总得有办法把正常工作日的这一团乱麻理清楚。我们越来越开始想，如果我们能和智能体更像同事一样协作，而不是更像软件一样操作，会怎样？这基本上就是 Grok Bot 很多设计的设计纲要。

turns.en: So to carry on that theme for a little bit, four things I wanted to call out here around agents as colleagues. And why this distinction is so important, I think, is because it's a lot of the inspiration behind the design of Grok Bot and how it works and how we're thinking about the road map too. So we think that colleagues really focus more on tying tools together to produce outcomes. Obviously connectors and MCPs and integrations have been a really strong and important part of the agent story across the industry. I think what's exciting here is making it so that you can tie those tools together to get work done. And so I think that's just a really important part of the story. I think long-running context and memory is really important here. Routines are really important here. And so thinking of first-class ways to do those in the product is really great. Colleagues remember what you do, like you work with them, they remember what you do. And so having that be a part of the solution is really important.
turns.zh: 那么沿着这个主题再讲一会儿，关于“智能体即同事”，我想点出四件事。为什么这个区分这么重要？因为它是 Grok Bot 设计、运作方式以及我们对路线图思考的很多灵感来源。我们认为，同事更专注于把各种工具串起来、产出结果。显然，连接器、MCP 和集成一直是整个行业智能体叙事中非常有力且重要的一部分。我觉得这里令人兴奋的是，让你能把这些工具串起来把活干完。所以我认为这是整个叙事中非常重要的一部分。我认为长时运行的上下文和记忆在这里非常重要。例行程序在这里也很重要。所以在产品里把这些做成一等公民，真的很棒。同事会记得你做的事，你和他们共事，他们记得你做了什么。所以让这成为解决方案的一部分非常重要。

ts.sec: Grok Bot as an Agent with a Computer

turns.en: I think colleagues are independent, and so making sure agents can be independent — calling back this idea of agents having their own computers, their own devices to do things on, their own software to go work with. And then finally I just think getting the messaging to feel right is a really important part of this. When I DM Kevin on Slack I'm rapid-fire messaging and sometimes throwing in some memes and emojis. I think there's something about that experience just being really fun that makes it feel like you're working with a colleague. So hopefully these themes make sense for those of you who had all the ones in the chat at the beginning from having used Grok Bot. Hopefully you've seen some of this. But I guess that brings us to: well, what is Grok Bot? And I want to simplify this after all of those words into two things. If there are sort of two things that you're using when you're talking about Grok Bot, or when you're talking about it with your friends and colleagues: the first is that it's an agent with a computer. And I think we're really excited about the computer part of this. It sort of gives the agent its own machine, its own environment to operate in, just like I was talking about. And it really just feels like texting a colleague who has its own computer. And the second is that your team of bots really are AI teammates. They're AI teammates that you can give real work to. They finish jobs end to end. They come back when they're stuck, and they function just like colleagues. And I've been pretty excited to see a lot of folks on X and other places talking about how Grok Bot seems to be more of a doing agent. So really excited for that to continue to be what we build.
turns.zh: 我认为同事是独立的，所以要确保智能体也能独立——回到这个想法：智能体有自己的电脑、自己的设备去做事，有自己的软件去协作。最后我觉得把消息传递的感觉做对，也是非常重要的一部分。我在 Slack 上给 Kevin 发私信时是连珠炮式的，有时还会甩几个梗图和表情。我觉得那种体验本身就很有趣，让你感觉像是在和一位同事共事。所以希望这些主题对你们这些一开始在聊天里刷了所有关键词、用过 Grok Bot 的人来说是说得通的。希望你们已经看到了一些。但我想这就引出了：Grok Bot 到底是什么？我想在说了那么多之后把它简化成两件事。如果你们在谈论 Grok Bot、或者跟朋友同事聊起它时，有两件事：第一，它是一个有电脑的智能体。我觉得我们对其中“电脑”这部分非常兴奋。它给了智能体自己的机器、自己的运行环境，就像我刚才说的。它真的就像在给一位有自己电脑的同事发消息。第二，你的机器人团队真的是 AI 队友。它们是你可以交付真实工作的 AI 队友。它们端到端完成任务，卡住时会回来找你，运作起来就像同事一样。我很兴奋地看到 X 和其他地方有很多人在说，Grok Bot 似乎更像是一个“做事”的智能体。非常期待这继续成为我们所构建的东西。

turns.en: Yeah, I think one of the things that we wanted to incorporate into Grok Bot is thinking about working with your best colleague or your best coworker or teammate. What is that like? Well, they're generally very proactive. They have a bias to action. They're able to take real action based off of your guidance. They learn on the job. And so we try to incorporate a lot of those principles directly into the product.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得我们想融入 Grok Bot 的一点，就是去思考和你最好的同事、最好的搭档或队友共事是什么感觉。那是什么样的？他们通常非常主动，有行动偏好，能根据你的指引采取真实行动，他们在工作中学习。所以我们试着把很多这样的原则直接融入产品。

turns.en: Yeah. And I think there are some fun ways too, like you can train them to do certain things and kind of teach them as if you would teach someone you're working with.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得还有一些有趣的方式，比如你可以训练它们做某些事，像教一位和你共事的人那样去教它们。

turns.en: Absolutely. Very cool.
turns.zh: 完全同意。非常酷。

turns.en: Do you want to walk us through what the team looks like?
turns.zh: 你要不要带我们过一遍这个团队是什么样的？

turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. So for the course of this demo we're going to run through a few of the really exciting PM-specific use cases, but this really generalizes for any type of product builder. And so as we go through, be thinking about your own workflows, things that you could potentially automate, different bots that you could potentially build, and we can talk about those in the chat and Q&A at the end. One of the things that I found Grok Bot to be very helpful with is keeping me focused. So I have this concept of the attention list, which is not necessarily what are my strict priorities going into the week or the day, but more like where is my attention. And so I like to think about Grok Bot as sort of sitting on top of my shoulder, being able to review all of the emails coming into my inbox, see what I'm responding to, see the different Slack threads that I'm actually engaging with, maybe the Slack threads that I need to know about but am missing, and curate this attention list that can then be used in different ways. And we can talk about how that can be a filter to keep you focused, how that can be diffed against your priority list so that you can understand where your priorities may diverge from where your time is actually going, and there are a lot of really interesting ways in which you can start to use this attention list to really guide your work. The other is, for the blocking and tackling of new product development, being able to very quickly research a bunch of different contexts. As Roshan mentioned, being a product manager, there can be context which lives in Notion, in Slack, in Gmail, and many other surfaces — your support tools, your CRM, right? And so being able to have an agent, a colleague that you can work with who can help you collect that, synthesize that, and formulate that into new product directions — very exciting, and we'll go deep into that use case. And then of course we also need to be able to ship. We need to be able to deliver new products to market. And so we'll talk about some of the workflows and agents that we have built to help us accelerate shipping. So we're going to go through the team that we have built. This is a combination of things that Roshan and I and the product team over at SpaceX AI have found to be very useful for product management. So let's meet the team. First we have Kora. Kora is our chief of staff. You can think of Kora doing all of the chief of staff things: figuring out what is most important both for us and the team, being able to reduce the distractions and block some of the things, maybe auto-respond to some of the questions that are coming in, and helping keep us focused and organized both personally and as a team. The next is Emily. Emily is an engineering manager. Emily has been coached and taught not to actually write code — like a good engineering manager — but instead to manage a team of engineers. And so these engineers are able to both learn from existing code and PRs that we have historically pushed across SpaceX AI, and learn some of the best practices, encode some of the skills from some of the best engineers across SpaceX AI, to be able to work just like an engineer. We also have Ashley. Ashley's probably my go-to throughout the day, being able to ask questions of our data. So Ashley has access to our data lake and our data warehouse and a bunch of different user insight and user research repositories. And so you can ask very broad and general questions and Ashley is going to be able to build you that right chart or that right slide or that right insight to be able to answer your question. And as a PM throughout the day, many questions will come up, and being able to have somebody that you can just DM and get an answer back really quickly has been exceedingly helpful. Pete — PM Pete — is our little product assistant, and so will help with a lot of our RFC and product requirement doc writing. He can also run that research, coordinate across these different agents, and really help us build a high-functioning product. Or we have our designer, Pixel. Talk about Pixel.
turns.zh: 好的，没问题。在这次演示中，我们会过几个非常令人兴奋的、产品经理专属的用例，但这其实可以推广到任何类型的产品构建者。所以在我们讲的过程中，请想想你自己的流程、你可以自动化的东西、你可以构建的不同机器人，我们可以在聊天和最后的问答环节聊这些。我发现 Grok Bot 非常有用的一点，是帮我保持专注。所以我有一个“注意力清单”的概念，它不一定是进入这一周或这一天的严格优先级，而更像是我的注意力在哪里。我喜欢把 Grok Bot 想象成坐在我肩膀上，能够审阅进入我收件箱的所有邮件，看看我在回复什么，看看我实际参与的 Slack 讨论串，也许还有我需要知道但漏掉的 Slack 讨论串，然后整理出这份注意力清单，再以不同方式使用它。我们可以聊它如何作为过滤器让你保持专注，如何把它和你的优先级清单做对比，从而理解你的优先级可能在哪里偏离了你时间实际花的地方，有很多非常有趣的方式可以开始用这份注意力清单来真正引导你的工作。另一个是，在新产品开发的基础攻坚上，能够非常快速地研究一堆不同的上下文。正如 Roshan 提到的，作为产品经理，上下文可能存在于 Notion、Slack、Gmail 以及许多其他界面——你的支持工具、你的 CRM，对吧？所以能够有一个智能体、一位可以共事的同事，帮你收集、综合这些信息，并把它转化为新的产品方向——非常令人兴奋，我们会深入讲这个用例。当然，我们还需要能够发布，需要能够把新产品推向市场。所以我们会聊一些我们构建的工作流和智能体，帮助我们加速发布。我们要过一遍我们构建的团队。这是 Roshan 和我以及 SpaceX AI 的产品团队发现对产品管理非常有用的东西的组合。那么，来认识一下团队。首先是 Kora。Kora 是我们的幕僚长。你可以把 Kora 想成做所有幕僚长该做的事：弄清楚对我们和团队来说最重要的是什么，能够减少干扰、挡掉一些事情，也许自动回复一些进来的问题，帮助我们在个人和团队层面保持专注和有条理。接下来是 Emily。Emily 是一位工程经理。Emily 被训练和教导不要真的去写代码——就像一位好的工程经理那样——而是去管理一个工程师团队。这些工程师既能从我们历史上在 SpaceX AI 推送的现有代码和 PR 中学习，也能学习一些最佳实践，把 SpaceX AI 一些最优秀工程师的技能编码进去，从而能像工程师一样工作。我们还有 Ashley。Ashley 可能是我一天中的首选，能够对我们的数据提问。Ashley 可以访问我们的数据湖和数据仓库，以及一堆不同的用户洞察和用户研究库。所以你可以问非常宽泛、笼统的问题，Ashley 会为你构建正确的图表、正确的幻灯片或正确的洞察来回答你的问题。作为产品经理，一天中会冒出很多问题，能够有一个人你直接发消息就能很快得到答案，这极其有帮助。Pete——PM Pete——是我们的小产品助手，会帮忙写很多 RFC 和产品需求文档。他也能跑那些研究，在这些不同智能体之间协调，真正帮我们构建一个高效运作的产品。还有我们的设计师 Pixel。聊聊 Pixel 吧。

turns.en: Yeah, I've been spending a lot of time working with Pixel actually.
turns.zh: 是的，其实我最近花了很多时间和 Pixel 一起工作。

turns.en: Yeah, I think design is one of those things that's really hard to get right with LMS and with AI tools. But I actually created Pixel inspired by a recent newsletter post from Lenny. There was a really great designer who posted a design system there, and I took that and put some of the context into Grok Bot, and you can supplement that with other design best practices. I think it's been one of the more fun ways to do design. Pixel has access to Figma, of course, so it can get into Figma and help make designs and slides, and also has access to our design system so that when we want to make something that matches the Grok Bot brand or matches other parts of the SpaceX AI brand, there's a really strong starting point and a really strong set of skills that Pixel's built over time to understand how to be creative and flexible and just be a great AI designer.

turns.zh: 好，非常好。看起来 Emily 实际上给我派了一个任务，要我去解除某位工程师的阻塞。看起来我这边需要做一个审批。

turns.en: And I think this is a good example where these types of handoffs—agents are really trying to be as active as possible on your behalf, but they can sometimes run into access issues or need your help to log into a tool that you use. And we want to equip our agents with the exact same tool set that we have access to so they can be most productive. And so we'll often get questions from the team here asking me to log in or whether they can have access to a particular tool that would make their work even more productive.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是一个很好的例子，说明这类交接——智能体确实在尽量替你主动做事，但它们有时会遇到访问权限问题，或者需要你帮忙登录你用的某个工具。我们希望给智能体配备和我们完全相同的工具集，这样它们才能最高效。所以我们经常收到这边团队的问题，让我去登录，或者问能不能访问某个特定工具，好让它们的工作更高效。

turns.en: Yeah, I think it's really helpful, as we talked about earlier, to make sure everything's connected. Obviously over the course of writing software, depending on a feature you're writing, you might need to be able to validate those in different ways. And so looks like our engineers are cracking away here.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得正如我们之前聊到的，确保一切连通真的很有帮助。显然在写软件的过程中，取决于你在写什么功能，你可能需要用不同方式去验证它们。所以看起来我们的工程师正在埋头推进。

turns.en: One thing I'll also mention that we didn't talk about much earlier is you can do all of this on mobile, right? So we saw that mockup of Grok Bot on mobile voice, but I'll often do this on the go. If I have an idea for a feature, I used to pull up a notes app and then wait till I got back at my desk and then type that into a prompt and then write a doc. But I can kick off this entire engine when I'm just on the go. I can talk into Grok Bot with the speech-to-text flow and maybe soon a voice flow. But really being able to access this anywhere and on any device, I think has been a really huge unlock. Sometimes inspiration strikes at the end of a meeting and you just want to be able to kick off an idea or kick off a prototype, and once you have the system set up, you can really go from zero to prototype really, really quickly. So very cool.
turns.zh: 还有一点我之前没怎么提到，就是这一切都能在手机上完成，对吧？我们看到了 Grok Bot 在手机语音上的那个原型，但我经常在路上就这么做。如果我有一个功能的想法，以前我会打开笔记应用，然后等回到工位再把它敲进提示词，再写一份文档。但现在我在路上就能启动整个引擎。我可以对着 Grok Bot 用语音转文字的流程说话，也许很快就能用语音流程。但真正能在任何地方、任何设备上访问它，我觉得是一个巨大的突破。有时候灵感在会议结束时突然冒出来，你就想马上启动一个想法或一个原型，而一旦系统搭好了，你真的能非常非常快地从零到原型。所以非常酷。

turns.en: So it looks like Eileen and Emily—
turns.zh: 所以看起来 Eileen 和 Emily——

turns.en: Who's Eileen?
turns.zh: Eileen 是谁？

turns.en: Eileen's one of our engineers.
turns.zh: Eileen 是我们的一位工程师。

turns.en: —and Larry are all coordinating on this work. And so looks like they are looking into the best way of implementing pool hint. And so this is just a great example here of really the autonomy and ways in which Grok Bots can coordinate their work, work together on some of these larger features.
turns.zh: ——还有 Larry，都在协调这项工作。看起来他们正在研究实现 pool hint 的最佳方式。所以这正是一个很好的例子，体现了真正的自主性，以及 Grok Bot 们如何协调工作、在这些更大的功能上协同合作。

turns.en: Yeah. And if you want to set up something like this, I think you're seeing that a bunch of different people or agents are being pulled into the chat. And that's because the way that Emily is set up and these engineers are set up is that they know they can tag each other. And so over time, as Emily has grown in her role as the EM here, she's learned that she can task out certain things to sub-agents or other agents, that she can loop in folks to help delegate work and then be able to review that work. So sort of creating a task-and-reviewer paradigm. And then also be able to test features independently as well. So in this case, we didn't have to tell Emily to go and tag these other bots, but that sort of—
turns.zh: 是啊。如果你想搭建类似的东西，我想你能看到，一堆不同的人或智能体被拉进了聊天。这是因为 Emily 和这些工程师的设置方式，让它们知道自己可以互相打标签。所以随着时间推移，Emily 在这个 EM 角色上不断成长，她学会了可以把某些事情派给子智能体或其他智能体，可以拉人进来帮忙分派工作，然后再审阅那些工作。也就是形成了一种“任务—审阅者”的范式。然后还能独立测试功能。所以在这个案例里，我们并没有让 Emily 去给这些其他机器人打标签，但那种——

consensus.en: Agents need their own environments to verify work and achieve better outcomes.
consensus.zh: 智能体需要自己的环境来验证工作并取得更好的结果。

consensus.en: The chat box is limiting for agentic work; agents should feel like colleagues, not software.
consensus.zh: 聊天框对智能体式工作有局限；智能体应像同事，而非软件。

consensus.en: Multiple specialized agents with scoped memory outperform a single general agent.
consensus.zh: 多个具有范围记忆的专用智能体胜过单个通用智能体。

consensus.en: Routines automate agent tasks and maintain tool connectivity for proactive work.
consensus.zh: 例程自动化智能体任务并保持工具连接，以实现主动工作。

consensus.en: Agents are good at prompting and coordinating with other agents, sharing context behind the scenes.
consensus.zh: 智能体擅长提示和协调其他智能体，在后台共享上下文。

consensus.en: Clean data foundations and canonical tables are essential for trusted agent insights.
consensus.zh: 干净的数据基础和规范表对于可信的智能体洞察至关重要。

contrarian.en: Product management is becoming software; everyone can now think like a PM.
contrarian.zh: 产品管理正在变成软件；现在每个人都能像产品经理一样思考。

contrarian.en: Agents as colleagues require independent computers, long-running memory, and fun messaging.
contrarian.zh: 智能体作为同事需要独立的计算机、长期记忆和有趣的 messaging。

contrarian.en: Engineering managers should not write code but manage teams of coding agents.
contrarian.zh: 工程经理不应写代码，而应管理编码智能体团队。

contrarian.en: The future of coding may focus on outcomes and agent coordination, not reading code.
contrarian.zh: 编码的未来可能关注结果和智能体协调，而非阅读代码。

contrarian.en: Attention lists that shadow you are more useful than traditional to-do lists.
contrarian.zh: 影子式注意力列表比传统待办列表更有用。
